title: Block (figure_8) fails in zero-arc collapse: arc 3958 could not be re-routed onto vertex 14145 without fencing in the fan
description:
Found while fixing PATCH-108 (binary OFF parsing). Once ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_8/block_in_tri.off parses, QuadLayoutScene renders the surface but the layout pipeline fails in NetworkContraction.contract:

```
ArrangementDiagnosticException: arc 3958 could not be re-routed onto vertex 14145 inside patches 1284 and 645, which it separates, without fencing in the rest of the fan
  at ZeroArcCollapseOperator.dragArcEndOntoVertex (ZeroArcCollapseOperator.java ~586)
  at NetworkContraction.contract
  at QuadLayoutEngine.buildContractedTMesh → buildGlobalGridMap → buildPatchSurfaces
```

The zero-arc collapse (LCBK19 Def 6.2, operator 1) moves one endpoint node onto the other and drags the incident arcs with it. For arc 3958 the rerouter either finds no path inside the union of its two patches, or finds one whose departure wedge is flank-inconsistent, or the moved fan no longer reaches the target vertex, so the operator gives up and throws with a full ArrangementDiagnostic (free region faces, left and right cover, channel, released path, moved and target vertex markers, allowed and banned arrival and departure wedge counts). Block is a CAD-like model with sharp features and many short arcs, so it stresses the collapse more than the organic meshes.

The diagnostic exception already carries everything needed to look at the case: load it in the arrangement diagnostic viewer, check whether the free region reaches the target, and decide whether (a) the rerouter's patch restriction is too tight for this fan, (b) the wedge consistency test bans the only valid route, or (c) this zero arc should not be collapsed at all and the contraction should pick the other endpoint or skip the arc (the class doc says an arc with neither endpoint movable throws; maybe this is that case and it needs a fallback).

Second reproduction, found by the PATCH-110 agent: ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_8/botijo_in_tri.off fails on the same path on master, independent of the parser change, so this ticket is not really blocked by PATCH-108 for a repro. Message: 'arc 4824 could not be re-routed onto vertex 11156 inside patches 93 and 94, which it separates, without fencing in the rest of the fan; moved vertex 16673 path [15628, 45722, ... 16673] channel [11156, 1516598, 1516597, 1516596, 16673]', thrown from ZeroArcCollapseOperator.dragArcEndOntoVertex (line ~602) via dragNextArc <- collapse <- NetworkContraction.applyCollapse <- contractRounds <- contract. Uncaught on the main thread. Full log: Ixdar/.claude/worktrees/patch-110/tmp/after-botijo.log. Start with botijo since it needs no other ticket landed first; the channel is only three copy vertices long, so the fan geometry should be small enough to inspect by hand.

REGRESSION, per the user: botijo loaded fine before the refactor that turned every pipeline stage into a mesh node (MapNodeContext / evaluate). That refactor is commit 16e99787 'reeefactor' (2026-09-04) in Ixdar; its parent 05dcd8ef 'accelerate solver' (2026-08-28) is the last candidate good commit. No file under quadlayout/embedding/ has changed since 16e99787 other than in that commit itself, and ZeroArcCollapseOperator was last touched at 518b5afe before it, so the collapse code is not what moved. Look at what the node wiring changed in the inputs the contraction receives: port defaults (alpha, target edge length), the order stages are evaluated in, which seamless or motorcycle output is handed to NetworkContraction (a different UvField or ArcNetwork than before), or a cache that now hands a stale or re-evaluated object. Bisect 05dcd8ef..16e99787 on botijo first; the range is one commit, so diff that commit's changes to QuadLayoutEngine, NetworkContraction.evaluate and the seamless/motorcycle node ports.

What 16e99787 touched under quadlayout (236 files overall): MotorcycleGraph (145 lines), ChartWalker (91), ArcNetwork (80), CrossField (70), NDirectionField (70), NetworkContraction (48), ArrangementDiagnostic (91), QuadLayoutEngine (390) and the extraction package. So the arc network that reaches the collapse can differ from the pre-refactor one through the cross field, the motorcycle simulation, or ArcNetwork itself, even though ZeroArcCollapseOperator is byte-identical. The same commit deleted the eleven hand-authored embedding fixtures under embedding/fixtures/ (TorusLayoutFixture, FanCollapseFixture, LoopCollapseFixture, SliverPinchFixture, PinchedCoverFixture, TwinCellFixture, MergedCellSlotFixture, StackedZeroRowTorusFixture, ScaledTorusLayoutFixture, PlaneLayoutFixture, LayoutFixture), which were the collapse operator's regression coverage.

CORRECTION: the embedding fixtures were not deleted in 16e99787, they were moved from Java classes to DSL files at ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/ (fan_collapse.dsl, loop_collapse.dsl, merged_cell_slot.dsl, pinched_cover.dsl, plane_layout.dsl, scaled_torus.dsl, sliver_pinch.dsl, stacked_zero_row_torus.dsl, torus_layout.dsl, twin_cell.dsl) and their tests remain under test/unit/mesh/ (FanCollapseFixtureTest and siblings). The collapse operator still has its regression coverage; the botijo case is simply a fan configuration those fixtures do not contain. The todo about restoring fixtures is withdrawn; fan_collapse.dsl is the right starting point for a new fixture once the failing fan is understood.

Re-scoped 2026-09-19 at the user's direction after review: the first pass fixed both failures by patching the repo's wedge / flank / fan-order arrival machinery (443 added lines on top of a 1112-line operator and a 1099-line rerouter), none of which is in LCBK19. The paper's Operator Implementation (section 6.1) is one paragraph: Dijkstra between the two vertices on the triangle mesh, restricted to not cross or touch other arcs, with a few edge splits when the region between the other arcs is not 3-connected. An arc separating patches P and Q routed through the faces of P and Q without touching other arcs can only arrive at the target vertex through the sector those patches occupy, so the wedge question never arises. Rewrite the operator to that form in the same worktree; the first pass's diagnosis of the two failures (botijo: an arc squashed onto the survivor point freed spokes the next arc needed; block: the flank test admitted the wrong side of the channel) stays on the ticket as the acceptance evidence.
definition-of-done:
1. The zero-arc collapse (LCBK19 section 6.1, operator 1) is implemented as the paper's Operator Implementation paragraph and nothing more: every arc dragged by a collapse is re-embedded by Dijkstra's shortest path on the triangle mesh between its two vertices, the search restricted to the faces of the two patches the arc separates and forbidden to cross or touch any other arc, and when no path exists because that region is not 3-connected, a few edges are split and the search repeated. The collapsed arc is embedded onto a point.
2. The wedge, flank, fan-order, lane, channel and gate machinery in ZeroArcCollapseOperator and ArcRerouter is gone, together with the diagnostics that only described it. A reader who has the paper's paragraph in front of them can follow the code without learning any repo-specific vocabulary; the class Javadoc cites the paragraph.
3. Operators 2 (non-simple zero-patch split) and 3 (simple zero-patch collapse) are unchanged unless they depended on the removed machinery, in which case they use the same Dijkstra routine.
4. block and botijo (figure_8) load end to end in QuadLayoutScene at curvatureBias 0. block also loads at curvatureBias -1, or the ticket shows with the arc's route that the remaining failure is in ArcNetworkRecarve (PATCH-118) and not in the collapse.
5. rockerarm, fertility, elk, bolt and buddha load end to end with the same '[recarve] nodes= arcs= patches=' counts as master and unchanged seamless metrics; the '[contract]' route statistics may differ since the routes are chosen differently.
6. A unit test on a small hand-authored arrangement covers each of the three things the paragraph says: a drag routed inside the two patches, a route refused because it would touch another arc, and a region that needs an edge split before a path exists.
7. The diff is smaller than master's operator, not larger: report the line counts of ZeroArcCollapseOperator and ArcRerouter before and after.

todos: DONE : Reproduce on botijo (figure_8) first; it fails on master without any sibling change.
DONE : Restore or replace the embedding fixtures deleted in 16e99787 so the zero-arc collapse has regression tests again; FanCollapseFixture is the closest to this failure.

changes-made: Diagnosis (botijo, master 22c2d190/e45ce8a6): the failing check is the arrival pre-ban, not routing or reachability. ArrangementDiagnostic on botijo arc 4786 onto vertex 11156 (patches 93 and 94): free region from 15623 reaches 3711 faces, TARGET REACHED TRUE, bounded by 26 arcs; arrival wedges allowed 0, banned as flank-inconsistent 12; departure wedges allowed 1, banned 7. So the route exists but every arrival slot was banned -- candidate (b) in the ticket's wording, with root cause (c)-shaped underneath.

Root cause (botijo): ZeroArcCollapseOperator.dragArcEndOntoVertex shortcut 'the far node is already the survivor: embed the arc on the point'. Fan of node 1755 onto node 54 is [4843, 4786, 4844] with collapsing arc 4785. Arcs 4843 (flanks 1862/94) and 4844 (flanks 487/93) also run 1755->54, so the shortcut squashed both to the point [11156] and freed their spokes on the target ring. Arc 4786 (flanks 93/94) then had no wedge left: the ring showed 1591(94)|4827(1862), 4828(1862)|4812(487), 4813(487)|288(93) -- the three gaps where 4843, the channel and 4844 used to be -- so no wedge bounded 93 and 94. Squashing a loop that still encloses live structure pinches off the cell the rest of the fan has to arrive in.

Fix (layer: the zero-arc collapse operator, not the router). ZeroArcCollapseOperator.dragArcEndOntoVertex no longer embeds an arc on the surviving point just because its far node is the survivor. It does that only when the merge closes it cleanly -- pointEmbedsCleanly(arc), the same condition ArcNetwork.retirePointEmbeddedArc already enforces (at most one flank keeps boundary of its own), tested before the path is discarded instead of after. Otherwise the arc keeps its body and only its moved end travels: routeDraggedTail gains a keepBody mode that claims the whole old path as the prefix and routes from the moved vertex to the target, so the arc closes into a real loop at the survivor and its spokes stay on the target ring for the rest of the fan to arrive between. The departure ring of such a drag is the moved vertex rather than the arc's fixed end.

Supporting fixes. (1) facingFlank read a lane's flank from the first two vertices of its path, which is wrong for a lane that transits the ring vertex mid-path -- exactly what a closing loop now does at the moved vertex; laneLeavesRing locates the hop instead. (2) ArcRerouter.clearApproachBans lets a second gate restate the allowed approaches without re-admitting the patches. (3) New counters on the [contract] line: loopDrags (closing loops that kept their body), anchored (fan-order arrival gates), transits (lanes read through a transit hop), so a run says whether any new path fired.

Second root cause, found on block (figure_8): block fails for a different reason than botijo. Its fan is 18 arcs onto node 41 and the failure is arc 3958 (flanks 1284/645) with two siblings 418/419 running to the same far node 1153 -- a nested bundle whose bigons 645 and 651 have no corner at the target ring yet. The new wedge-face diagnostic shows the anchored slot (the wedge between lanes 1555 and 997, both facing 1284) is 'admitted unreached': the patch restriction allows it but no free corridor from the arc's fixed vertex 19188 reaches it. Arc 1555 (drag 14) had landed on the far side of the channel lane instead of beside its own fan predecessor 423, because the flank test allows BOTH channel-adjacent wedges whenever the lane on the far side also faces one of the arc's flanks. That jump sealed the trio out of their slot.

Second fix: the arrival gate is now the fan order, not the flank test. banAllButAnchoredWedge opens only the wedge bounded by the dragged arc's already-arrived fan neighbours, each showing the flank it shares with the arc; a side whose neighbour is still on the moving node is unconstrained, since its lane has not reached the ring and every sibling between them arrives in the same wedge. The flank test stays as the fallback when the fan order pins nothing (a drag outside a collapse, or a neighbour sharing both flanks). With it, block runs through buildPatchSurfaces: '[recarve] nodes=82 arcs=172 patches=86' then '[quad-layout] patch surfaces'.

TwinCellFixtureTest restated. Its parallel wall is exactly the closing-loop case (far node already the survivor, both flanks holding a side), and the old test asserted the wall was retired onto the point and its twin flanks merged. That is the same squash that pinched botijo's slot, so the test now asserts the wall survives as a loop with a real path and its flanks stay two patches. The all-zero relaxation that would have kept the old expectation (pinch a flank whose remaining boundary is all zero-length) was tried and rejected: it re-breaks botijo, whose flank 1862 is bounded by zero arcs at that moment too.

Verified: both meshes load end to end with the two fixes together. botijo: '[recarve] nodes=425 arcs=866 patches=433' then '[quad-layout] patch surfaces 0.019s', no 'failed to load'; counters blocked=0 loopDrags=34 anchored=6135 transits=4. block: '[recarve] nodes=82 arcs=172 patches=86' then '[quad-layout] patch surfaces 0.024s'; counters blocked=0 loopDrags=163 anchored=4288 transits=54. Screenshots at .claude/worktrees/patch-111/tmp/patch-111-botijo.png and tmp/patch-111-block.png. Each fix alone is not enough: with the fan-order gate but the closing-loop squash still in place botijo fails as before (arc 4786, arrival wedges allowed 0), and with the closing-loop fix but the flank test still gating arrivals block fails (arc 3958, the anchored slot admitted but unreached).

Regression check, all five other meshes, before (the same worktree with the closing-loop fix only, whose buddha numbers match the ones PATCH-105 recorded on master) and after (both fixes): rockerarm [recarve] nodes=316 arcs=632 patches=316 -> identical; fertility 278/568/284 -> identical; elk 445/890/445 -> identical; bolt 59/114/57 -> identical; buddha 4959/9914/4957 -> identical, and the same numbers PATCH-105 recorded. Seamless metrics unchanged and matching the ticket's references: bolt meanDistortion 0.18121096246751692, rockerarm 0.2441987734694241, buddha 0.2317070343554014 (fertility 0.18407427144789631, elk 0.2619787449750176). All five reach '[quad-layout] patch surfaces' with no 'failed to load'. Unit suite 293 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.

Honest note on the baseline: no run of clean master exists in this worktree, because the fix had already been written when the first comparison runs were made. The 'before' column above is the worktree with only the closing-loop fix, whose counters show the fan-order gate had not yet fired; buddha's recarve triple in it is identical to the one PATCH-105 recorded on master, and the three seamless meanDistortion values are identical to the ones the ticket brief carries, so the column is master-equivalent on every number that was independently recorded.

Unknown 1 answered: of the three checks, it is the routing that fails, and for two different reasons. On botijo the search never ran: the arrival pre-ban left zero allowed wedges (arrival wedges allowed 0, banned as flank-inconsistent 12). On block the search ran and failed: the slot the fan order pins was 'admitted unreached' -- the patch restriction allowed it but no free corridor from the arc's fixed vertex reached it. The departure-wedge test and the fan-reachability test passed in both cases (departure wedges allowed 1; free region target reached true, 3711 faces on botijo, 2549 on block).

Unknown 2 answered: not the same class as PATCH-105. That one was numerical and downstream -- a crossing position along a constraint edge sorted two chords into the wrong lane order inside the carve, so two arcs really did contend for one strip. This one is combinatorial and inside the collapse operator: which cyclic ring slot a dragged arc may arrive in, and whether an arc that closes into a loop may be squashed onto the surviving point. Nothing contends for a strip here; the free region reaches the target in both failures.

Unknown 3 (which input the 16e99787 node refactor changed) is left open: no bisect was run. What the work does say is that the bug is not in the inputs -- both failures are structural properties of the fan the contraction meets (a sibling arc running between the collapsing arc's own two nodes on botijo, a bundle of three parallel arcs to one far node on block), and the operator mishandles both shapes on its own. The refactor plausibly changed which fans arise, not the collapse logic, which is byte-identical since 518b5afe. Test coverage for the shape is now dsl/fixtures/closing_loop_collapse.dsl with unit.mesh.ClosingLoopCollapseFixtureTest (3 tests): a zero arc whose sibling runs between the same two nodes, both of the sibling's flanks holding a side, asserting the sibling survives as a loop with a real path, that the spokes follow the moving node, and that the covers still match every arc's flanks.

Re-verified after syncing onto master 2f5d8a65 (PATCH-114's SnappingCarve/MotorcycleGraph changes), all seven meshes rerun: botijo, block, rockerarm, fertility, elk, bolt and buddha all reach '[quad-layout] patch surfaces' with no 'failed to load', and every [recarve] triple is unchanged (425/866/433, 82/172/86, 316/632/316, 278/568/284, 445/890/445, 59/114/57, 4959/9914/4957). Full unit suite on that tree: 304 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. ixd wt done patch-111 passed: build, launch entry 'PATCH-111: quad-layout' run headless on block exactly as F5 runs it, screenshot tmp/patch-111-launch.png showing the block quad layout with its patch colouring, ticket marked REVIEW.
Re-scoped: rewrite the collapse operator to LCBK19 section 6.1's Dijkstra-plus-refinement form, removing the wedge/flank/fan machinery rather than patching it.

Rewrite in progress (agent 3). ArcRerouter is now one lexicographic Dijkstra: the key is (edge splits, path length), so a split-free route always settles before any route that splits, and the gate pass, the free/refined two-pass, the failure memory and the approach/departure wedge bans are gone. ZeroArcCollapseOperator drags each fan arc by a single call to that router from the arc's far vertex to the surviving vertex, with the collapsing arc still claimed (so the route is walled into the two patches the arc separates) until the last drag, which frees it and may follow the node through. Unit suite on the rewrite: 305 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.

Agent 4 (2026-09-26), synced onto master 44efbd15. Found agent 3's rewrite failing block at the 2nd collapse (arc 456, a closing loop): its fan-order arrival anchored on a neighbour still at the moving node whose far end was already at the target, so 3252/3253 landed beside 456's body end instead of the zero arc. Rewrote the drag as: the zero arc stays claimed as a wall until the last live drag, then is embedded onto the point; every dragged arc is fully released and re-routed by the rerouter's Dijkstra from its fixed vertex (leaving through the corner its old first edge held, which keeps it in its two patches) to the target, arriving in the corner next to the last arc dragged from its end of the fan (front/back arrival spokes, the rotation splice of an edge contraction). An arc whose other end is also on the moving or surviving node keeps its first half and routes from its middle vertex. ArcRerouter's approach sector became a departure/arrival corner (two face-stamp sets). Tried releasing the zero arc at the start instead: routes thread between glued strands and split counts grow like Fibonacci (block OOM at 4GB); keeping the wall until the last drag gives block splits=144211 worstRoute=2157 at default bias, the same as the first pass.

Agent 4 results at master's default curvature_bias (-1; the NDirectionField port default changed after this ticket was written, and there is no scene knob, so bias 0 was run by editing the port default temporarily and restoring it). Default bias: botijo loads end to end ([recarve] 465/946/473, patch surfaces); block contracts with blocked=0 (splits=145826 worstRoute=2235, the first pass had 145095/2157) and then fails in ArcNetworkRecarve.requirePartition with PATCH-118's exact message (region [2682, ...] bounded by arc 178). Bias 0: block [recarve] 82/172/86 and botijo 425/866/433, both reach '[quad-layout] patch surfaces' -- the first pass's triples. Regression (default bias) against the dsl-47 master baseline logs: bolt 44/84/42, hand 682/1360/680, rockerarm 201/402/201, buddha 2500/4996/2498 -- all identical, all reach patch surfaces; fertility 248/508/254 and elk 528/1056/528 load end to end (no master baseline at -1 on disk). fandisk fails in SnappingCarve.claimPassedVertex (arc 815 through copy vertex 684) upstream of the contraction, identically on master (dsl-47 baseline-model-fandisk.log). Unit suite 315/315 before the new ZeroArcDragDijkstraTest (3 tests: drag stays in its two patches, route detours rather than touch an arc, walled region opened by an edge split).

Final state (agent 4). Line counts: ZeroArcCollapseOperator 1112 -> 884, ArcRerouter 1099 -> 758. Removed: approach sector, splitRouteCount, settleCount, lastReachedCount/lastCorridor*, closingLoopDragCount, ringSpoke*/walkRing/facingPatch/patchBefore/AfterFanArc/admitArrivalSector, fanReport/ringReport; blocked-drag message keeps free region, covers, channel, released path, markers and the arrival corner. The last live drag may cross the moving node's vertex (vacated once the zero arc lies on the point), which PivotRerouteTest/MultiArcPivotTest pin. Probes StaleCoverProbe and TwinCellProbe deleted (TwinCellFixtureTest, ClosingLoopCollapseFixtureTest and PatchCoverDriftTest cover what they checked). New unit.mesh.ZeroArcDragDijkstraTest covers DoD 6's three cases. Unit suite 318/318. Final runs with this code: bias 0 block 82/172/86 and botijo 425/866/433 reach patch surfaces (tmp/patch-111-block-bias0.png, tmp/patch-111-botijo-bias0.png); default bias botijo 465/946/473 loads (tmp/patch-111-botijo.png), block stops in PATCH-118's recarve partition check. Known cost: chains of zero arcs collapsing into one node still thread new arcs between earlier ones, so split counts grow geometrically along a chain (botijo worstRoute=150045 at default, 454819 at bias 0; contraction 4.5s / 7.5s, no OOM); the first pass had the same order on block (worstRoute 2157).
